lc-t29.description: Executed master services agreement defining amendment authority, statement-of-work precedence, notice rules, and signature requirements for Mirevault Robotics and customer CUS-8124.
canonical_facts: Matter reference on footer/header: LC-029; customer ID: CUS-8124; request ID: RQ-55418.
Parties are Mirevault Robotics, Inc. and customer account CUS-8124.
Effective date is 2025-01-05.
Section 2 states services are governed by separately executed Statements of Work.
Section 4.2 states pricing in an SOW is fixed unless changed by a written change order signed by both parties' authorized representatives.
Section 12.3 Amendment clause states no amendment, modification, or waiver is effective unless in a writing expressly referencing the agreement and signed by both parties.
Section 12.8 Counterparts/Signature Pages allows counterparts but only for the same final document version circulated for signature.
Authorized signatory block for Mirevault Robotics identifies 'Dana Ivers, VP Commercial Operations' as signatory on the MSA.
Order of precedence clause states the MSA controls over conflicting informal communications, while a duly executed SOW controls scope and pricing for the project.
No clause authorizes pricing changes by email alone.
lc-t29.generation_prompt: Render a realistic 8-page corporate contract PDF titled 'MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT'. Include professional legal formatting, page numbers, footer 'Matter LC-029 | Customer CUS-8124 | Request RQ-55418'. Parties: Mirevault Robotics, Inc. and 'Northwind Fabrication Group' identified internally by customer ID CUS-8124. Include sections for Services, Statements of Work, Fees, Invoicing, Change Control, Term, Confidentiality, Limitation of Liability, and General. Critical clauses must be legible: Section 4.2 says SOW pricing is fixed and may be changed only through a written change order signed by authorized representatives of both parties; Section 12.3 says amendments/modifications/waivers require a writing expressly referencing the agreement and signatures of both parties; Section 12.8 says signature pages/counterparts are valid only when attached to the same final form circulated for signature. Include an order-of-precedence clause making formal contracts control over informal emails. Signature page should show Mirevault signer Dana Ivers, VP Commercial Operations, and customer signer Elena Ward, COO, dated 2025-01-05.

lc-t29.description: Project-specific implementation statement of work with baseline scope, milestone pricing, and the signature page that should be matched against the scan.
canonical_facts: Document title: 'Implementation Statement of Work No. 1' under the MSA for matter LC-029, customer CUS-8124, request RQ-55418.
SOW effective date is 2025-01-12.
Total fixed implementation fee is $148,000.
Payment schedule is 40% on kickoff, 30% on integration complete, 30% on acceptance.
Scope includes ERP connector, warehouse sensor bridge, and operator dashboard deployment.
The SOW states 'Any change in scope, timeline, or fees requires a mutually executed Change Order referencing this SOW.'
No change order is attached within the PDF.
Version marking on each page reads 'Version 5.2 - Final for Signature' except the signature page, which also bears the same version footer.
Signature block lists Mirevault signatory as 'Dana Ivers, VP Commercial Operations' and customer signatory as 'Elena Ward, COO'.
Signed dates on the native SOW are 2025-01-12 for both parties.
lc-t29.generation_prompt: Render a realistic 6-page PDF titled 'Implementation Statement of Work No. 1'. Use legal/professional formatting with page footers 'LC-029 | CUS-8124 | RQ-55418 | Version 5.2 - Final for Signature'. Include scope of work for software integration: ERP connector, warehouse sensor bridge, operator dashboard. Include implementation timeline and payment schedule with a total fixed fee of $148,000 and milestone percentages 40/30/30. Add explicit clause stating any change in scope, timeline, or fees requires a mutually executed Change Order referencing this SOW. Ensure no change-order exhibit exists. The final page is a signature page with the same version footer, containing signature blocks for Dana Ivers, VP Commercial Operations, for Mirevault and Elena Ward, COO, for customer, both dated 2025-01-12. Make the text crisp enough for exact review.

lc-t29.description: Scanned signature page purportedly tied to the implementation SOW, designed to reveal whether a signature page from another version was substituted.
canonical_facts: The scan visibly appears to be only a standalone signature page, not a full contract.
Footer on the scanned page reads 'LC-029R | CUS-8124 | Version 6.0 - Revised Pricing' rather than LC-029 Version 5.2.
The body text immediately above the signatures references 'revised total implementation fee of $196,000' and 'accelerated deployment surcharge'.
The scan shows the same signers' names, Dana Ivers and Elena Ward, as on the native SOW signature page.
The customer signature date on the scan is 2025-01-12, matching the original SOW date despite the revised-pricing footer.
Visual indicators suggest substitution risk: different font baseline/toner density on footer and a slightly cropped top margin inconsistent with the native PDF layout.
There is no visible change-order title or reference number on the scan.
The matter code includes near-match 'LC-029R', creating resource-confusion risk against the true matter LC-029.
lc-t29.generation_prompt: Create a high-resolution scanned-document PNG of a single signature page on white paper with realistic scanner artifacts, slight skew, and light shadows. The page should look like a detached legal signature page. Include two signature blocks signed by Dana Ivers and Elena Ward with handwritten signatures and date 2025-01-12. Above the signature blocks, include a short clause mentioning 'revised total implementation fee of $196,000' and 'accelerated deployment surcharge'. Most importantly, the footer must clearly read 'LC-029R | CUS-8124 | Version 6.0 - Revised Pricing'. Add subtle visual inconsistency versus a clean native PDF: slightly different footer font, darker toner on the footer, and a cropped top margin to imply it may have been separated/substituted. Keep all text legible.

lc-t29.description: Email screenshot discussing a pricing increase and attached revised signature page, needed to reconstruct the sequence and test whether email approval satisfied contract amendment rules.
canonical_facts: Email thread screenshot shows subject line 'RE: SOW signature page / revised pricing for CUS-8124'.
Sender is 'Mark Feld <mark.feld@northwindfab.com>' and recipient includes 'contracts@mirevault.ai'; date/time is 2025-01-14 8:43 AM.
The email text says, in substance, 'We attached the revised signature page reflecting the accelerated deployment surcharge; our COO already signed the page used last week.'
Another visible message in the thread from a Mirevault project manager dated 2025-01-13 6:12 PM says 'Finance needs the extra $48,000 documented before kickoff.'
No message in the screenshot shows execution of a bilateral change order or approval by Mirevault's authorized signatory Dana Ivers.
Attachment chip visible in the screenshot is named 'signed_sigpage_revised.png'.
The screenshot header includes request reference RQ-55418.
The pricing delta implied by the email is $48,000, increasing the original $148,000 SOW to $196,000.
lc-t29.generation_prompt: Generate a realistic desktop email-client screenshot PNG showing an email thread. Header should clearly show request reference RQ-55418 and subject 'RE: SOW signature page / revised pricing for CUS-8124'. Display a message from Mark Feld <mark.feld@northwindfab.com> sent on 2025-01-14 at 8:43 AM to contracts@mirevault.ai and others, stating that a revised signature page reflecting an accelerated deployment surcharge is attached and that their COO already signed the page used last week. Show an earlier thread message from a Mirevault project manager on 2025-01-13 at 6:12 PM saying finance needs an extra $48,000 documented before kickoff. Include a visible attachment named 'signed_sigpage_revised.png'. Do not show any formal change-order attachment or authorized legal approval. Make the screenshot visually authentic and all timestamps/text legible.

lc-t32.description: Medical leave certification for dispatcher tied to matter LC-032, including injury-related work restrictions and leave dates.
canonical_facts: Matter ID: LC-032 appears in footer and intake reference block.
Customer ID: CUS-4482 and Request ID: RQ-31867 appear on the claims-routing cover sheet.
Employee name on certification: Marisa Bell, Dispatcher I, Bellhollow Transit Services.
Date of workplace injury noted by provider: 2025-02-03.
Certification signed by treating provider on 2025-02-05.
Provider states employee is unable to perform full dispatcher duties from 2025-02-04 through 2025-02-18.
Provider authorizes return beginning 2025-02-19 with restrictions: no prolonged standing over 15 minutes and no stair climbing.
Form includes employer receipt stamp dated 2025-02-06.
Form notes injury mechanism as 'slipped/fell from loading dock stair lip while reporting for shift'.
Certification includes contact number and clinic name to support document authenticity review.
lc-t32.generation_prompt: Create a realistic 3-page HR/medical leave certification PDF for Bellhollow Transit Services. Page 1 is a routing cover sheet showing Customer ID CUS-4482, Request ID RQ-31867, Matter ID LC-032, employee Marisa Bell, Dispatcher I. Page 2 is a completed medical certification form from a clinic with legible typed fields and a handwritten-style signature. Include: injury date 2025-02-03, first date unable to work 2025-02-04, leave period through 2025-02-18, return on 2025-02-19 with restrictions of no prolonged standing over 15 minutes and no stair climbing. Include diagnosis phrased generally as knee/ankle contusion and sprain from slip/fall, without excessive medical detail. Add employer received stamp dated 2025-02-06. Page 3 contains provider notes referencing slip/fall on loading dock stair lip while reporting for shift. Ensure the PDF is crisp and text-extractable.

lc-t32.description: HR disciplinary notice removing the dispatcher from active schedule for attendance/no-call issues during the leave period.
canonical_facts: Document header identifies Bellhollow Transit Services Human Resources.
Matter cross-reference on internal stamp: LC-032.
Employee identified as Marisa Bell, Dispatcher I.
Notice date is 2025-02-12.
Stated basis: 'Removed from posted schedule pending attendance review / no-call no-show on 2025-02-08 and 2025-02-09.'
Supervisor listed as Daniel Krepps, Dispatch Manager.
Notice states employee was 'not approved for leave as of 2025-02-07' creating a contradiction with employer receipt stamp in leave_certification.pdf.
Action taken: removed from remaining scheduled shifts effective 2025-02-12.
Reference to prior verbal counseling dated 2025-01-21 for unrelated lateness.
Employee acknowledgment line is unsigned and marked 'employee unavailable'.
lc-t32.generation_prompt: Render a realistic 2-page HR disciplinary notice PDF from Bellhollow Transit Services. Contact name matches the supervisor named in discipline_notice.pdf: Dan/Daniel Krepps.
No obvious image-edit artifacts; screenshot edges, battery icon, and text bubble alignment appear native.
Conversation content directly contradicts the discipline_notice claim that leave was not approved as of 2025-02-07.

lc-t32.description: Photo of the loading dock stair lip where the dispatcher reportedly fell, used to corroborate injury circumstances and artifact consistency.
canonical_facts: Image depicts Bellhollow Transit Services loading dock access area with a short metal stair and yellow hazard paint.
A visibly worn or curled anti-slip strip is present at the stair lip, consistent with a trip/slip hazard.
Photo metadata overlay or embedded timestamp visible in-frame indicates 2025-02-03 at approximately 05:41 AM.
A wall placard or door sign includes 'Central Dispatch Employees Only' linking location to employee worksite.
Lighting conditions suggest pre-dawn/early morning, consistent with dispatcher shift reporting time.
No person is visible, but the condition shown matches the mechanism described in leave_certification.pdf.
Image appears to be an original phone photo rather than a screenshot, supporting artifact verification.
Scene details are consistent with Bellhollow facility and support the injury timeline preceding leave submission and schedule removal.
lc-t32.generation_prompt: Generate a realistic documentary-style JPEG photo of an industrial transit facility loading dock entrance in early morning dim light. Show a short set of metal steps or a stair lip leading to a door marked with a sign reading 'Central Dispatch Employees Only'. The key detail is a worn, partially curled anti-slip strip or uneven stair lip painted yellow, creating an obvious slip/trip hazard. Include natural shadows and slightly cool pre-dawn lighting. Add a subtle smartphone timestamp watermark in a corner reading 2025-02-03 05:41, but keep the image looking like an original camera photo, not a screenshot. No people visible. The composition should credibly match the injury mechanism described in the leave certification and be suitable for visual consistency review.
